title: Statues of 'Ain Ghazal
description: Villagers of a large Neolithic settlement make plaster figures of people, among the oldest large statues known.

title: Mesha Stele
description: King Mesha of Moab sets up a stone recording his victories over Israel, the longest inscription of its age from the region.

title: Nabataeans repel Antigonus
description: The Nabataeans defeat forces sent against them by Antigonus I, the first dated event in the history of the people who built Petra.

title: Rome annexes the Nabataean kingdom
description: On the death of the last Nabataean king the emperor Trajan turns his kingdom into the province of Arabia.

title: Hadrian visits Gerasa
description: The city builds a triumphal arch for the emperor's visit, at the height of the prosperity of the cities of the Decapolis.

title: Madaba Map
description: A floor mosaic laid in a church shows the Holy Land and Jerusalem, the oldest surviving map of the region.

title: Battle of Mu'tah
description: A force sent by Muhammad fights the Byzantines and their Arab allies east of the Dead Sea, the first clash between the Muslims and the Roman Empire.

title: Battle of Fahl
description: The Muslim army defeats the Byzantines in the Jordan valley and goes on to take the towns of the region.

title: Qusayr 'Amra
description: An Umayyad prince builds a desert lodge and bathhouse whose wall paintings are the best preserved of early Islamic art.

title: Kerak Castle begun
description: The Crusader lord Pagan the Butler begins a great castle east of the Dead Sea to control the road between Damascus and Egypt.

title: Kerak falls to Saladin
description: The castle surrenders after a long siege, ending Crusader rule east of the Jordan.

title: Burckhardt reaches Petra
description: The Swiss traveller Johann Ludwig Burckhardt, disguised as a Muslim pilgrim, is the first European for centuries to see and describe Petra.

title: Circassians settle Amman
description: Circassian refugees from the Russian Empire are settled by the Ottomans among the ruins of Amman, the beginning of the modern city.

title: Capture of Aqaba
description: Forces of the Arab Revolt led by Auda Abu Tayi and advised by T. E. Lawrence take the Red Sea port from the land side.

title: Emirate of Transjordan founded
description: Abdullah, son of the Sharif of Mecca, forms a government under British protection in the lands east of the Jordan, the beginning of the Jordanian state.

title: Independence
description: The parliament of Transjordan proclaims Abdullah king after Britain ends its mandate by treaty.

title: Jordan annexes the West Bank
description: Parliament approves the union of the two banks of the Jordan, including East Jerusalem, taken in the war of 1948.

title: Assassination of Abdullah I
description: A Palestinian gunman shoots the king as he enters the mosque for Friday prayers.

title: Hussein becomes king
description: Parliament removes King Talal on grounds of illness and his son Hussein, aged sixteen, begins a reign of forty-six years.

title: Glubb Pasha dismissed
description: King Hussein removes the British commander of the Arab Legion and puts the army under Jordanian officers.

title: Battle of Karameh
description: Israeli forces raid a base of Palestinian fighters in the Jordan valley and meet resistance from them and the Jordanian army, which raises the standing of the Palestinian groups.

title: Black September
description: The Jordanian army fights the Palestinian armed groups based in the kingdom, which are driven out to Lebanon by the following summer.

title: Jordan gives up its claim to the West Bank
description: King Hussein cuts legal and administrative ties with the territory in favour of the Palestine Liberation Organization.

title: Peace treaty with Israel
description: Jordan becomes the second Arab state to make peace with Israel, settling the border and the sharing of water.

title: Death of King Hussein
description: The king dies after forty-six years on the throne and is succeeded by his son Abdullah II.

title: Amman hotel bombings
description: Suicide bombers of al-Qaeda in Iraq attack three hotels and kill about sixty people.

title: Zaatari refugee camp opens
description: A camp opens for Syrians fleeing the civil war and grows within a year into one of the largest refugee camps in the world.
